Third party

The third_party app: a simulated third-party service, which receives each approved article through its own API.

third_party.models

The third_party app’s model: the simulated third party’s record of each approved article it receives.

class third_party.models.ThirdPartyArticle(*args, **kwargs)[source]

An approved article, as received by the simulated third party.

It is the third party’s own record, so it stores plain text copies of the article’s details, with no links to the application’s other tables.

Variables:

  • title – The article’s title.

  • content – The article’s text.

  • journalist – The author’s username.

  • publication – The publication’s name, or blank for an independent article.

  • created_at – When the article was created in the application.

  • received_at – When the third party received the article.

third_party.serializers

The simulated third party’s serializer, for the approved articles it receives.

class third_party.serializers.ThirdPartyArticleSerializer(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Checks an approved article sent to the simulated third party, and turns the saved record back into JSON.

Every field sent is required: the title, content, journalist’s username, publication’s name, and the article’s creation date and time. The publication is null for an independent article.

Variables:

publication – The publication’s name. It can be null for an independent article, which is stored as blank.

validate_publication(publication)[source]

Turns the null publication sent for an independent article into a blank one, since the model’s publication can be blank but not null.

Parameters:

publication – The publication’s name sent, or None for an independent article.

Returns:

The publication’s name, or an empty string for an independent article.

third_party.views

The simulated third party’s API: the endpoint that receives approved articles.

third_party.views.receive_article(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

The simulated third party’s endpoint, which receives approved articles as JSON and saves them.

The third party expects a valid API key in the X-API-Key header, checked against the THIRD_PARTY_API_KEY setting. The view checks the key itself, so the usual login and permission checks of Django REST Framework (DRF) are turned off. A request without the right API key, or with missing or invalid fields, is refused with a message saying why.

Parameters:

request – The API request, with the article as JSON.

Returns:

201 Created, with the saved article; 401 Unauthorized if the API key is missing or not valid; or 400 Bad Request, with each missing or invalid field.

third_party.admin

The simulated third party’s admin page.

Registers the articles received by the simulated third party, with Django’s default admin pages.
